_about: The reel backlog, made in order. The Sunday planner (coming next) adds to it from the content calendar, new articles and tools, and what worked last week. Keep about 70% on the buyer's problems (traffic loss, fixes, reporting) and 30% on AI and automation. format: fix or myth. clip (optional): a clip id from assets/clips.json that must be used.

topics.topic: Search Console now shows how often you appear in AI Overviews and AI Mode
topics.angle: Search Console, Performance, the new generative AI report (global since 31 Aug 2026): impressions, pages, countries, devices for AI Overviews and AI Mode. Open it, compare with the normal Search results report, note the pages that appear in AI answers but lost clicks. Sources: developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports

topics.topic: Google answers your own brand name with AI now: 8 in 10 branded searches
topics.angle: DemandSphere: about 26% of tracked branded queries had an AI Overview in early September 2026, 82% by 29 September; Ahrefs: 82.9% of 92.5M US desktop branded crawls on 29 September. Check: Search Console, Query filter with your brand, Compare September to August, watch CTR not position.

topics.topic: The spam update that would not end
topics.angle: Search Status Dashboard: September 2026 spam update started 24 Sept, still ongoing; March took 19h30, June 2d1h, August 2d16h. Don't judge a fix until the end date is posted; check the date your drop started before blaming it.

topics.topic: Find the pages quietly losing traffic, in Search Console, in under a minute
topics.angle: Performance report, compare the last 3 months with the previous 3, Pages tab, sort by the clicks difference. The pages at the top are the ones to fix first. Traffic loss is quiet: nobody gets an alert.

Myths people act on when an old post drops: that changing the date fixes it, that a drop always means a Google penalty, that you should delete old posts that lost traffic. Facts: what actually helps (update what searchers now want, check who outranks you, merge or redirect thin duplicates).

topics.topic: Striking distance keywords: the queries already close to page one
topics.angle: In Search Console, filter queries by average position between 8 and 20, sort by impressions; those pages need one focused improvement, not a new article. Show it in Flowra's striking distance report.

topics.topic: "Crawled, currently not indexed": what it means and what to do
topics.angle: Search Console, Indexing, Pages. Google saw the page and chose not to index it. Check it's not a thin near-duplicate, make it clearly better than what ranks, link to it from strong pages, then request indexing once. Requesting again and again does nothing.

Myths: two pages ranking for one keyword is always bad; the fix is always to delete one. Facts: it's a problem when they swap places and split clicks; check in Search Console by filtering the query and looking at the Pages tab; merge and redirect, or make each page answer a different intent.

topics.topic: Win the featured snippet for a question you already rank for
topics.angle: Find question queries where you rank in the top 5 (Search Console, filter queries containing how, what, why). Put a 40 to 50 word direct answer right under a heading that repeats the question. Lists and tables for steps and comparisons.

topics.topic: A content audit in three decisions: keep, update, or merge and delete
topics.angle: Export pages with 12 months of clicks. Keep what grows. Update what drops but still gets impressions. Merge or delete what gets neither, redirecting to the closest page. Our full guide is on the Flowra blog.

Myths: you can't see traffic from ChatGPT; AI answers never send clicks. Facts: in GA4, Traffic acquisition, session source shows chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai and others when they send visits; it only counts visits that arrive, not answers that didn't send a click. Flowra's AI traffic tracking reads those referrers.

topics.topic: Did your content update actually work? How to measure it honestly
topics.angle: Note the date you changed the page. Wait about two weeks for Google to settle. Compare the same length of time before and after. Check the whole site moved too, or you'll credit a seasonal swing to your edit. It's a before and after comparison, not an A/B test.

topics.topic: The SEO client report clients actually open
topics.angle: Lead with what changed and why, then what you're doing next; one chart per point; share a link that always shows the current report instead of a PDF that goes stale. Show Flowra's shareable client report link with the agency's own branding.

topics.topic: Myths about what makes content rank
topics.angle: Myths: longer articles always rank better; you need to publish every day; a higher keyword density helps. Facts: match what the top results cover for that search; a better update to an existing page often beats a new one; write for the question, not a density number.

topics.topic: Check whether ChatGPT's crawler can actually reach your site
topics.angle: Your robots.txt can allow GPTBot and your host can still block it. We found our own host returned HTTP 429 to GPTBot at the edge while other AI crawlers passed. Test: fetch a page with the GPTBot user agent, check the status code, ask the host to allow it.
